## Fix round 2: secret check no longer rejects genuine random secrets; typecheck, lint and npm test pass on Node 24 and 22

**Commit:** `2ee385c` on `feat/intelligence` in `C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build`, on top of round 1's `1063b72`. Local only, with the trailer. I staged only `api/src/config.ts` and `api/test/config.test.ts`; the tester's uncommitted test-acceptance files were not touched.

**What changed:** `secretEntropyProblem` used to reject any secret where one character made up more than 25% of it. It now rejects only when chance would almost never produce that many repeats of one character: for n characters from an alphabet of A, it rejects when A · P(Binomial(n, 1/A) ≥ maxCount) < 1e-12. Alphabet sizes are 16 for hex, 64 for base64/base64url and 94 for other printable text; base64 `=` padding is not counted. The probability is computed exactly, so a truly random secret is wrongly rejected with probability below 1e-12. New exports: `DOMINANCE_FALSE_REJECT_BOUND`, `dominanceTailBound(n, A, k)` and `dominanceRejectCount(n, A)`.

The smallest repeat count that is now rejected:

| Secret format | Length | Rejected at | Chance a random secret is rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| hex-64 | 64 | 25 | 4.5e-13 |
| hex-40 | 40 | 20 | below 1e-12 |
| base64-48 | 64 | 16 | 1.9e-13 |
| base64-32 / base64url-32 | 43 | 14 | 1.7e-13 |

**Decision for you:** I did not use your example formula (mean + 8·standard deviation). That estimate badly understates the real probability when the alphabet is large, so it cannot meet the 1e-12 target. For base64-48 it would reject 9 of one character in 64, which happens to about 4.5e-5 of random secrets; for hex-64 the rate would be about 1.8e-8. The function comment explains this.

**Other checks unchanged:** values that are too short for their alphabet, repeated patterns, fewer than 8 distinct characters, and placeholders are still rejected. `'a'*64`, `'ab'*32`, `'0123456789'*7` and `'changeme'*8` are all asserted as "is a repeated pattern".

**Tests added in `api/test/config.test.ts`:**
- The existing test with 1000 random secrets per format is kept.
- A seeded set (same bytes every run) of 1000 each of hex-64, base64-48, base64-32 and base64url-32.
- A separate exact calculation confirming the four thresholds, that one count lower would not meet 1e-12, and that it agrees with `dominanceTailBound`.
- A boundary check: 24 of one character in a 64-char hex secret is accepted, 25 is rejected.

**Flake check:**
- The randomized test passed in all 20 repeat runs.
- A temporary stress run of 200,000 random secrets (50,000 in each of the four formats) produced 0 rejections; I deleted that test file afterwards.

**Results** (CI env, Node 24.21.0 and portable Node 22.23.3, both the same):

| Command | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| typecheck | 0 | |
| lint (nothing excluded) | 0 | |
| npm test | 0 | shared 134, api 346, web 62 |

**Docs:** no operator doc described the old 25% rule, so I changed none.

I appended a "Fix round 2" section to `implementation.md` and a BUILD_COMPLETE entry to `mailbox.md` in `C:/Users/mariu/.[REDACTED:high_entropy]`. Logs are in the session scratchpad as `fixr2-n24-*.txt` and `fixr2-n22-*.txt`.
